rules.title: Identify effective project requirements
rules.text: Extract candidate requirements from the effective project specification, including requirements intended for later stages.
checks: Recheck the original proposal and designated protocols, supplements, clarifications and review decisions; use compression as supporting context.
Use existing project designations and decisions to establish adoption, effective version and replacement scope. Do not request the same confirmation again.
Keep draft, suggested, withdrawn or superseded requirements outside the active collection. Refer unresolved adoption or replacement questions to PRC008.

rules.title: Extract decision-relevant project obligations
rules.text: Extract the source-supported requirements that govern how this project must be carried out, including constraints that limit the intended result.
checks: Look for required actions, prohibitions, permitted-use boundaries, fixed analysis choices and required decision gates concerning data, methods, interpretation or deliverables.
Retain every explicit consequential obligation, including conditional and later-stage requirements. Key means decision-relevant, not a fixed number of top-ranked rules.

Keep pure objectives, descriptive facts, assumptions and optional suggestions outside the formal rule collection. If the source requires an assumption to be used, extract that obligation and link the compression-owned assumption.

Interpret normative intent in context, not by keywords alone; do not create requirements from customary PK practice, literature choices or inferred scientific needs. An empty rule collection is valid when the source review supports it.

Apply explicit annotation definitions and positive/negative boundary examples. First decide whether a source statement is an adopted requirement, recommendation, non-rule or unresolved requirement; then fill its fields. Cue words direct attention but do not decide the classification.

rules.title: Extract a complete actionable requirement
rules.text: Represent each obligation together with the source-stated actor or target, required or prohibited action, applicability, conditions and exceptions.
checks: Extract linked qualifications across paragraphs, tables, footnotes and cross-references as one connected requirement; keep AND/OR, only-if and obligation strength intact.
For requirements containing scientific definitions, use the complete applicable preservation profile and PK binding appendix referenced by this contract.
Do not turn an unknown detail into a required value. If an upstream fact or assumption is missing or inconsistent, return a source-linked correction request to compression.

Fill only source-supported actor, action, target, normative form, source modality, workflow phase, deadline and frequency. Preserve multiple forms and linked alternatives; NOT_SPECIFIED is not permission to invent a value. Keep conditions, exceptions and observation windows in their existing dedicated fields.

rules.title: Bind each requirement to original evidence
rules.text: For every candidate rule, identify the original evidence that supports its full meaning and the project evidence that adopts it.
checks: Map each consequential clause to exact source spans, locations and relevant context; one source may support both meaning and adoption.
Record non-rule dispositions and their reasons in source coverage, using upstream fact and assumption references instead of recreating those catalogues.
Keep source-to-candidate links through organization so the final reviewer can inspect all contributing and contradictory evidence.

Bind each populated requirement field to exact admitted source spans. Include definitions and cross-paragraph qualifiers needed to interpret it. Cover every admitted source unit; relevant-context selection must not hide unselected obligations. A matching quotation proves location, not semantic support or project adoption.

rules.title: Annotate when and where the rule is used
rules.text: Give each extracted rule source-grounded applicability and usage timing so downstream tasks receive the requirements they need.
checks: Preserve stated analysis, dataset, biological, endpoint and exposure restrictions; assign consumer stages using the workflow catalogue and distinguish that routing from source-stated applicability.
Keep observation windows separate from required workflow phases, triggers and deadlines. Do not bring a deferred requirement forward.
Use an explicit unresolved routing or applicability status when information is insufficient; do not invent task or dataset IDs. Usage annotations do not establish compliance.

rules.title: Clarify only gaps affecting requirement extraction
rules.text: Identify unresolved authority, obligation meaning, contradictions or applicability that prevent a faithful rule package.
checks: Return a targeted question linked to the affected candidate and source, stating what decision depends on the answer.
Block publication when requirement meaning, adoption, conflict or essential applicability remains unresolved; assess the impact before downgrading any issue.
Keep later-stage scientific data gaps with needed_at and impact. They are not new obligations or automatic blockers for this extraction step.

rules.title: Check the final extracted rule collection
rules.text: Independently review the organized candidate collection against the original project materials and reviewed context before publication.
checks: Record faithfulness, completeness and global-conflict outcomes for the final rule wording; the checks may share one fresh reviewer invocation.

Verify bidirectional source-unit-to-candidate-to-final-rule coverage. Each explicit consequential obligation must be represented; each final rule must have support. NO_REQUIREMENT must not conceal a mapped obligation.
Check that organization retained all rule qualifiers and sources and that the collection is consistent with the relevant main.json objective, facts, assumptions and data-use constraints.
Return required context changes to compression. Publish only the unchanged reviewed collection after the host checks its mappings and output contract.
Assess requirement detection, slot binding and grounding separately. Review the host-organized final rule records and their source/candidate mappings; bind the decision to their content hash.

adopted_methods.title: GoLLIE: Annotation Guidelines Improve Zero-Shot Information-Extraction
Extraction of Information Provision Activity Requirements from EU Acquis
LLM-assisted Extraction of Regulatory Requirements: A Case Study on the GDPR

methodology.attribution: The category labels, PK examples, source-adoption decisions and integrated workflow below are project-specific design. The cited studies support individual techniques; none validates this PK proposal-to-rules pipeline.

logical_phases.name: Define the annotation task
logical_phases.procedure: Supply category meanings, inclusion/exclusion boundaries and a few relevant contrast examples before extraction. Use the project's input schema rather than relying on label names or model-specific keyword conventions.

logical_phases.name: Find candidate obligations
logical_phases.procedure: Inspect each admitted source unit with its parent context. Identify directive intent, scope and adoption separately; retain non-rule and ambiguous dispositions. Cue terms aid attention but must not be the only inclusion filter.

logical_phases.name: Fill requirement slots
logical_phases.procedure: Extract the action and its source-stated actor/target, force, conditions, exceptions and use timing. Keep related alternatives and qualifiers connected. An unspecified field stays unspecified.

logical_phases.name: Bind context and evidence
logical_phases.procedure: Link original clauses and any needed definitions, tables or cross-references from admitted sources. Distinguish evidence for meaning from evidence for project adoption. Inaccessible material becomes a targeted finding, not an inferred rule.

logical_phases.name: Organize and review the final collection
logical_phases.procedure: Use shared deduplication rules, retain source/candidate/final mappings and check missed requirements separately from unsupported additions, wrong slots and altered conditions. Use the existing final independent review.

classification.label: REQUIRED_ACTION
classification.definition: The effective project specification commits the analysis or workflow to an action, deliverable or choice.
classification.include: Explicit directives or unambiguous adopted project commitments, even without must/shall.
classification.exclude: Predicted future events, descriptive study methods and optional suggestions.

classification.label: PROHIBITION
classification.definition: The project forbids a stated action or use within a stated scope.
classification.include: Explicit exclusions, access/use restrictions and negative obligations.
classification.exclude: Statements that a result was not observed or a method was not used in a cited study.

classification.label: PERMITTED_USE_BOUNDARY
classification.definition: The project explicitly defines what use is allowed and under which limits.
classification.include: Restrictions such as use only for initialization or use only after approval.
classification.exclude: Do not turn permission to do something into a duty to do it.

classification.label: RECOMMENDATION_OR_OPTION
classification.definition: A suggested or optional action that has not been adopted as a binding constraint.
classification.include: Consider, could and preference language when context is genuinely optional.
classification.exclude: Do not discard a conditional mandatory instruction merely because it contains if or may.

classification.label: NON_RULE
classification.definition: A pure objective, descriptive fact, result, assumption or explanatory statement.
classification.include: Refer to the compression-owned context and record the non-rule disposition.
classification.exclude: An explicit instruction to use an assumption is a rule even though the assumption itself is not a verified fact.

classification.label: UNRESOLVED_REQUIREMENT
classification.definition: A potentially consequential obligation whose meaning, force, adoption or scope cannot be settled from the admitted evidence.
classification.exclude: A later-stage data gap with clear rule meaning is not automatically an extraction failure.

cue_terms.purpose: Non-exhaustive reading aids; no regex-only filter or keyword-based proof of obligation.
cue_terms.interpretation: Use sentence and document context. Preserve SHOULD/MAY strength, distinguish possibility from permission, and do not normalize ambiguous may not to a prohibition without evidence.

slot_guide.action: What must be done, avoided or limited.
slot_guide.actor_or_target: Who acts or what analysis, dataset, parameter or output is constrained.
slot_guide.normative_force: Source-stated obligation, prohibition, conditional permission or recommendation; never upgraded for formatting.
slot_guide.exceptions_and_alternatives: Retain exclusions, AND/OR structure and linked options.
slot_guide.scientific_scope: Use the canonical scientific preservation profile for relevant PK details.
slot_guide.usage_timing: Separate consuming stage and required phase from the scientific observation window.
slot_guide.evidence_and_adoption: Original source spans and project adoption references; they may be the same source.
slot_guide.missing_slots: Record the existing contract's explicit missingness state and raise a question only if the missing item changes interpretation or publication.

synthetic_examples.status: ILLUSTRATIVE_AUTHOR_WRITTEN_CASES; not study data, project instructions or a validated benchmark

cases.source: Use free-drug exposure for all PK/PD index comparisons.
cases.avoid: Do not apply the requirement to unrelated total-concentration PK fitting.

cases.source: The cited study used a two-compartment model.
cases.avoid: A reported model choice is not a project mandate.

cases.source: For this project, use the cited two-compartment structure, but do not import its parameter values.
cases.avoid: Do not infer permission to reuse parameters from adoption of a structure.
Do not require a third compartment or turn the suggestion into a release gate.

cases.source: If verified individual-animal data are available, estimate animal random effects.
cases.avoid: Do not invent individual IDs from group means or make the instruction unconditional.

cases.source: Literature parameters may be used only as starting values.
cases.avoid: Do not mandate literature initialization or permit fixed final parameter adoption.

cases.source: Use either candidate A or candidate B.
cases.avoid: Splitting must not create two simultaneous mandatory actions.

cases.source: Human binding data are reserved for final validation and must not be used during initial extrapolation.
cases.source_context: Synthetic adopted protocol; existence of such data is not assumed
cases.avoid: Do not require those data now or claim they have been supplied.

cases.source_context: Adopted project protocol without a definition of acceptable
cases.avoid: Do not invent an RSE, AIC, sample-size or convergence threshold.

methodology.execution: Detect then fill slots within one extraction call; use one fresh independent reviewer on organized final rules. No additional call per phase.
methodology.source_policy: Read all admitted source units with original context. Reuse source IDs in citations, never as task/dataset IDs. A quoted or draft obligation is not adopted solely because its document has a project role.

schema_mapping.NON_RULE: PROJECT_OBJECTIVE, LITERATURE_FACT or CONTEXT_ONLY; do not re-extract the full fact/assumption catalogue
schema_mapping.mixed_clause: Keep linked forms in one requirement.forms array; preserve AND/OR in text and conditions.

methodology.field_contract: For a PROJECT_REQUIREMENT, field_evidence must cover /text, every populated /requirement scalar, each /conditions and /exceptions entry, and populated biological /scope fields. Use NOT_SPECIFIED for absent scalars and [] for absent arrays. Empty requirement.forms and field_evidence on non-rules. Scope stages are workflow routing, justified separately by routing_reason.
methodology.host_limits: Exact quotes, mappings and valid schemas do not prove semantic correctness. The reviewer must check entailment, adoption, omissions and qualifiers.
